She will ask him to dance, as she always does, and he will do his duty and lead her to the floor, and know once more the sweet torture of holding her in his arms in a crowded room, every eye on him and her, searching for something to start the rumours they will repeat the next day. But he can only bear so much — he prays she will spare him yet another night of agony.

summary:
In the feverish port city of Attre, wealth and rot grow side by side.
Its guard is understaffed, its customs offices corrupt, and every faction in the city watches Commander Roderic of Valmora, a provincial noble from the Amell Mountains, waiting for him to fail.
When a shipment of rare pharmaceutical reagents is stolen from the powerful Veyr-Merreck Company, the crime first appears to be simple. But the precision of the theft, the quality of the stolen materials, and the silence surrounding the case convince Roderic that ordinary criminals are not behind it. With no one in the city he can fully trust, he secretly calls for help from the mountains.
Ivo Arlen arrives under the guise of a pharmacological consultant. In truth, he is a witcher of the hidden Guild of the Phoenix, a secretive order of alchemists, healers, and mutated hunters born from knowledge both noble and shameful. Ivo begins to follow a trail through Attre’s alleys, canals, dormitories, burned shops, forged records, and forgotten tunnels.

summary:
Pups are precious, it is imbued in their very being, in their instincts the moment they wake up with cat-slit eyes and the lingering bitter taste of herbs clinging to their tongue, even more so after the means of creating more pups are forever lost after the attempted sacking of their keep. It doesn’t matter that they prevailed and humans have since learnt not to bite the hands that protect them. Too many brothers, too many pups have been lost.
So when a foolish alderman dares to steal a vial of the few mutagens left right under their noses in a blasphemousblasphemousblasphemous attempt to create a witcher pup to exploit, well.
Suffice to say, the witchers of the Wolf school are pissed.

author: Karlethandra_Merthensa
fandoms: Wiedźmin | The Witcher - All Media Types
relationships: Lambert (The Witcher)/Milena de Roggeven (Accidental Warlord Series - inexplicifics)
characters: Milena de Roggeven (Accidental Warlord Series - inexplicifics)
summary:
The way she said things was weirdly familiar too.  Sayings Lambert hadn’t heard since he was damn young, but also that wasn’t that weird because Triss was older than him, so her knowing various older sayings wasn’t unexpected. But it- it stuck with Lambert, for some reason.  How she said them stuck too.  A cadence that… that hurt to hear, for some fucking reason. 
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Lambert had no family.
As far as he knew, they'd all died off to plague, or monster, or man sometime before he'd even gotten his medallion. The blood that carried the Potter name would die with him, and all other Potters of the continent could feel a little more special after.  Lambert didn't care; he hadn't claimed or even thought about his sire's second name in decades.
So yeah, Lambert had no  blood  family.  He had the Witchers, his brothers, and he had Milena. He even had the mages, because although they were typically terrible, at least Triss was nice and tried damn hard to be a good person.
It'd be nicer if she wasn't so damn  familiar  though.

summary:
Dedicated to Eredin Bréacc Glas, King of the Wild Hunt, self-proclaimed ruler of the Aen Elle, and, incidentally, the architect of my nightmares. That alone was enough to set this story in motion, a sign that someone was not entirely satisfied with his fate.
The elf like that, if washed, combed, and spared the coal-black eyeliner, though admittedly it had its own twisted charm, deserved many things. But not such an inglorious end.
What other path could there be? Interdimensional, of course. Threaded with the same ironic force the world of The Witcher prefers to call Destiny.
This is not a naive attempt to “save a red flag.” Calling him that would be an understatement. He is a full crimson banner of the Wild Hunt tearing across dying worlds.🚩🦅
👑Elven tyrants with no conscience at all are our deliberate choice.
A choice that inevitably leads to suffering and destruction... But is that all it leads to?
And yes, we will quietly discard the tired “BDSM maniac” caricature so common online. You are a king and a warrior. Your darkness is deeper, colder, and far more refined.🖤
Fly well through the Spiral, Sparrowhawk. And this time... try not to crash.

Crowned far sooner than you were ever meant to be, you learned quickly how to rule with a steady hand and careful distance, especially where mages are concerned. Generations before you distrusted their kind, and you have never seen a reason to be the first to change.
So when the court delivers a sorceress to stand at your side as advisor, you greet her with the same cold suspicion you have always reserved for magic and those who wield it.

There was a minor problem with Ithlinne's Prophecy.
Emhyr var Emreis was convinced it was about him.
Vilgefortz wanted power.

None of them were correct.
Geralt of Rivia was trying his best.
Sigismund Dijkstra was trying very hard to locate one missing bard before the Continent collapsed.
And Jaskier—
Jaskier wanted absolutely nothing to do with any of it, thank you very much.
He wanted songs. Stories and Adventure. A certain white-haired witcher and preferably in that order.
Unfortunately, Destiny had read the prophecy.
And, like everyone else, it enjoyed a good joke.

summary:
"If life could give me one blessing, it would be to take you off my hands!"
A long, pregnant pause lingers between them, wherein a small eternity passes before him in a handful of seconds. There's a wrench in his chest, where his heart should be, shattering to pieces. He might choke on it, the blood he knows should be slicking his throat and suffocating him. All very poetic, he decides, and fitting, for the end. Geralt is still looking at him, snarling, tension rolling off him in waves, teetering there on the edge of the cliff, and he makes his decision.
"Have it your way, then, Geralt."
Yellow eyes, furious and, if he should let himself indulge, afraid, are the last thing he sees as he takes a step back towards the edge and then he's falling, falling, and there is nothing but blue sky and fog and the edges of the mountains rising to meet him.
(Or: Jaskier makes a different decision, that day on the mountain. It all just sort of goes to shit from there, really.)

summary:
Geralt of Rivia never asked to be a king. Through a mix of human paranoia and witcher pragmatism, he ended up crowned the so-called Warlord of Kaer Morhen, a title he despises almost as much as the politics that come with it. Instead of fighting drowners, he’s fending off nobles with bribes and marriage proposals, all convinced the witchers are raising an army. When King Foltest suggests sealing a treaty through a political marriage, Geralt finds himself backed into a corner.
The chosen partner is Julian, charming on paper, sharper in truth, and half human. Geralt agrees only out of duty to his keep, Yennefer, and Ciri, knowing one wrong move might frighten his would-be husband to death. But surviving monsters is simple; surviving a marriage arranged by kings may prove the harder task. And if Geralt isn’t careful, obligation may become something far more dangerous: attachment.

Aleksander swallowed thickly, his throat suddenly dry. The most handsome man Aleksander had ever seen stood above him, with shoulder length dark and loose curls, a styled goatee and the prettiest green eyes Aleksander had ever seen in his life. His lips were moving, smoothing into a smile as he leaned onto his hand on the table. Aleksander blinked, his brain trying to catch up and move beyond handsome man as he started to speak -
No, not speak, he was singing. Singing along to the song playing over the speakers — which only now staring at the handsome stranger's lips could Aleksander understand was actually a song about a man asking another for their chair back.
Oh God, Aleksander was in his seat -

This the English version of my story "Widma z pogranicza", written in Polish. Enjoy! :)
On the eastern borderlands of Skavinia, covered in an ancient primeval forest, cranes cry out over the meadows, kingfishers dart above the river, and herds of mighty bison thunder through woodland paths. The landscape feels like something out of a painting by Renklod Delorene or Villem Tair-Nerr. The locals value tradition and peace above all else, and the regional cuisine—especially bigos washed down with the famous bizunka—strips away any trace of self-control. And when, on a sunny morning, the forest is fragrant and the birds sing together in chorus, it might seem as though you are in paradise.Too beautiful to be true? You’re right. This forest is a trap.What will Geralt and Jaskier discover within it? Where will the fox trails and wooden walkways through the marshes lead them? I’m afraid that this time, very close to our own reality. So it will be dark. But in this story you will also find a beautiful magical vixen, an extraordinary duel, the wise old granny Hałyna, and plenty of Polish music. Enjoy!

Fuck. When Coen started dragging him north, he’d just assumed it was coincidence. He’d brought the news that all the witchers were gathering together for a conference of sorts for the winter. Except now they were standing at the base of the mountain pass leading to Kaer Morhen and Lambert was finally realizing what was going to happen.
He’d spent decades away from this place. He’d hidden his medallion so no witchers even knew he was a wolf. And now every last one of them was going to be there on the day that he finally returned to the home where he was made. It wasn’t going to be a pretty sight.

Warlord Geralt z Rivii | Geralt of Rivia
summary:
Couvade syndrome: A condition where an expectant partner experiences physical and emotional pregnancy symptoms, such as nausea, weight gain, insomnia, and anxiety. It is considered a psychosomatic response to the partner's pregnancy, often peaking during the first and third trimesters. It is not a mental illness, but rather a real physical reaction to the life change, often lasting until childbirth.
In this case, it's our lovely Witchers experiencing varying symptoms in varying degrees of severity.

summary:
The first morning the flowers appeared, people were delighted by them. A lush spray of blush-pink blossoms that draped above the white marble lintel of a heavy wooden door, they looked like a miracle, a gorgeous mystery in the middle of the drab city. They were a bright, lush sweep of life in an otherwise lifeless world. Eyes widened and then crinkled with smiles that stretched cold-chapped lips and warmed hearts. Women on the way to and from the market found their baskets and burdens felt lighter. Men felt a joy in their steps as they passed. Children, for whom winter seemed like it had lasted half their lives, stood across the street and stared, itching to dig into the plush, soft petals and smell the scent of green growing things bruising against their fingers.
Those that passed too close to the door found that the cloying sweet scent of roses clung to their lungs, making their hearts beat faster and their blood rise with unnamed longing.

summary:
Only Geralt is out now. Everything feels muffled, only sharpened by the cold biting at his cheeks. It’s not ideal, with the snow reflecting the sky everything is still bright, and shadows are soft, blending into each other. With the snow already disturbed, all Geralt really can do is to remain at high alert. The potions he drank left a tang on the back of his tongue, putrid and nauseating, but every bit necessary. The streets have been decorated since the winter solstice with ribbons and branches tied together to form arches, and absolutely an obstacle for both hunters.
Too late, Geralt notices the shadows thickening around him, and a heavy weight carries him down. His foot slips, and his knee hits the frozen ground before that too is swept from under him. Claws dig into his shoulder, a hot breath hitting the side of his face, reeking of blood and decay. His grip falters, forcing the sword from his hand at the impact. The katakan has pinned him on his front in the snow.

summary:
He plays his role, now. He’s learned his lesson and he plays the role they all expect him to play. Silly bard. Ridiculous poet. Jester, and troubadour; the rousing laughingstock. A worthless joke.
He’s silly and he’s outrageous and he never cries, never, never cries, because crying isn’t part of the role he’s supposed to play. He doesn’t wake gasping for air he can’t find, doesn’t bite his fist to keep the pathetic sounds inside, doesn’t scream until he can’t scream any more, all the pent up angerandfearandrageandterrorandohgodspleasejustmakeitallstoppleasepleasepleasepleaseplease coming up and out. He doesn’t, because that’s not the role he plays. Can’t. Be the role he plays.
Because he’s the pawn. The lackey. The disposable piece that will one day be used up and discarded like the trash he was, is, and always will be.
Or:
After everything that's happened over the past several years, Jaskier finds himself going through the motions of life, longing for death. No one notices that he's just playing at being the grandiose bard he once was, a shadow of his former self. After all, why would they?
He's just a pawn.

The small kitchen is warm with residue heat from the oven. It also smells heavenly, and a pile of cookies are cooling on a tray temptingly close from where Jaskier is sat on the kitchen counter.
He helped, he totally helped, someone has to steal the batter and dice the chocolate, the two tasks he is trusted with in Geralt’s kitchen, and it has the added bonus of Geralt watching him lick his own finger clean.

The Path is lonely and Geralt is starved for touch and affection. He goes to bed with the bard in Posada to scratch an itch, expecting the bard to want to do horrible, violent things to him like most people do when they have an indestructible beast kneeling for them.
Instead the bard calls him nice things and doesn't leave when he's taken his pleasure and starts following him around the continent. Geralt is confused, thinking that Jaskier must be hiding some ulterior motive and bloody appetites but somewhere along the way they become friends.
Convinced that Witchers are unlovable creatures Geralt fights a hard inner battle with himself only to be faced with the most horrifying reality just as he is ready to let his guard down around the bard - Jaskier was worse than anyone else he'd ever taken to bed.

He had no experience with the dead, he realised, as he was cradling Jaskier's body in the river, letting the flowing waters wash away the blood. Those he buried were those who had no-one else, those who were destined to be forgotten by the sands of time, those whose lives meant nothing and deaths meant even less.
That was not Jaskier. Jaskier who had captured the heart of hundreds, Jaskier who loved and was loved freely, Jaskier who had changed the world with just his voice.
And yet it was still Geralt who wiped his face of blood with a damp rag. Who bandaged his stomach and dressed him in a clean chemise. It was Geralt who lay him down in the ground and kissed his forehead.
How unbelievably unfair.

Geralt draws his attention to the lute carefully set to the side of the bed: Jaskier’s pride and joy. Instruments, for Geralt, are entirely against his nature as a Witcher. Despite this, Geralt has secretly wondered what would happen if he were to pluck a string with his own hand; his hand that has only ever graced the hilt of a weapon. But here the instrument sits before him, a darling and intricate product of humanity. The instrument has no other purpose but to illuminate the human condition, the sorrows, and the passion. When Jaskier plucks those strings and sings his songs, Geralt could almost convince himself he feels such things. Of course, he would never say such a thing aloud, especially not to Jaskier.

He breathed in deeply, his hands trembling with the stupidity of what he was about to do. Jaskier had done some stupid things in his time but walking into the Brokilon Forest was by far the most idiotic thing the bard had ever done. 
But he knew what he was getting into when Yen told him where Geralt was taken following the disastrous battle at Thanedd. He knew what he had to do.

Jaskier adjusted the lute on his back, the city of Cintra on the horizon. He had not met any friends on his travels to the city, but then again, he hadn’t expected to do so. He was with several other bards, all responding to the call Cintra had made for bards to make a song cycle about Queen Cirilla’s reign. Even with his hasty exit from Redania, he managed to send a letter to a friend who he hoped would be a friendly face in the city, though they had not parted well.
The young queen was shrouded in mystery with a bit of infamy. Everyone knew that she was claimed by the Law of Surprise by the Butcher of Blaviken. The deranged witcher brought some of his witcher friends when Nilfgaard tried to conquer Cintra. Though Cirilla was only twelve at the time, her powers combined with the witchers were able to keep Cintra from the edge of defeat, though her grandmother still lost her life in the process. At the age of twelve, she was put on the throne, despite not being of age.

summary:
Soulmate marks are faint. These marks are an impression of a soulmate’s hand lines and fingerprints. These are curious markings that only some seem to have. It is suggested that chaos has its hand in those sentient beings with these intricate markings.
Although rare, it is not entirely unheard of that someone may have multiple soulmates. For Witchers who live entirely too long of lives, it might come as no surprise that eventually, Geralt and Eskel both found a new pattern of curls and grooves growing on their skin. Lambert’s seventeenth year brought the beginnings of a third set of whirls on each man’s body.
Those that Melitele blessed and specifically those that were never meant to be more than what they were born as, frightened humanity. For nobility to be blessed with Fate’s mark was not necessarily a sign of misfortune, but rather the potentiality that a Noble house would grow in strength because of its proximity to Chaos. However, three separate displays of Melitele’s touch tested the bounds of just how close to Chaos nobility wanted to be. Jaskier was lucky and unlucky in this respect.

What happens behind the scenes is my personal twist. Please note that "The Witcher” belongs to CD Projekt Red and Andrzej Sapkowski. This is a fan work written purely for fun and appreciation of the characters. Later edit: 30 chapters in and I have to admit that this current piece is, in fact, romance. Trying to put her life back together and find a way to move on after losing everyone she loved.
In 1272 AR, in Skellige, Cirilla Fiona Elen Riannon, Child of the Elder Blood, Lady of Space and Time, steps through a portal in the ancient tower of Tor Gvalch'ca. She goes to face the White Frost, a mysterious force that consumes entire worlds in ice and snow. Only a child of the Elder Blood can stop it, but Ciri has no idea what she will face on the other side.
Two young women from different worlds; Multiversal travelers, children of prophecy and queens of fallen kingdoms; will be brought together in the shadow of the Second Conjunction of the Spheres. summary:
“You said you wouldn’t let me die,” hissed the wraith with Jaskier’s face, its cold fingers closing around Geralt’s throat. “You promised!”
Geralt’s eyes snapped open. The night was quiet and still, with not even the slightest hint of wind to stir the leaves on the trees. His medallion was likewise still, but it lay beside his ear on the bedroll instead of on his chest, and the section of chain across his neck was chilly instead of skin-warm. He must have moved while he was dreaming and dislodged it.
---
Jaskier survived an ordeal that ought to have killed him, and seems to have come out the other end no worse for wear. So it would be silly for Geralt to still be having nightmares. Ridiculous, even. It would be the absolute height of foolishness to go days without sleeping when everything is fine.
Because everything is fine.

There stands a house near the end of the world, on a rocky shore where the North Sea becomes the Gulf of Praxeda and the south wind somehow blows colder than the north, shielded as land is by the Dragon Mountains.
[...]
The door is thrown open and the rider comes out of the darkness, snow blowing in before the door is jammed shut. The Witcher unwinds the face-covering scarf with a customary lack of care, dragging the fur cape down to reveal pale skin scared along the cheek, eyes green as emerald and white hair sticking out rebelliously from a thick braid broken by wind.
”I should have started earlier,” says Ciri as she shakes the snow out of clothes and hair.
Morvran says nothing. He closes his book carefully, stands up from his armchair and walks the five steps across the floor with the ceremony of a man walking up a temple nave beneath the eyes of the gods. He’ll serve no master but her.

When Jaskier accidentally gets blessed by a mischievous dryad, things take a romantic turn—every time he sings, people nearby erupt into dramatic confessions of love. It’s flattering at first… until the chaos starts.
Towns fall into emotional uproar. Goats follow him. And Geralt—stoic, grumpy, and extremely bad at feelings—becomes Jaskier’s reluctant bodyguard against wave after wave of magically lovesick villagers.

Geralt may not know the words—but he’s always had the tune.

Old jokes stumble back to life.
Old wounds rise with the wind.
And two hearts who never truly parted must relearn how to walk side by side.
In the quiet of snow-thick nights and soft touches rediscovered, they find warmth again — not in the dying embers of the fire, but in each other.

summary: When Geralt takes on a seemingly ordinary contract in a remote village, he expects a restless spirit. What he finds instead is something different entirely. The real monsters wear human faces, and their cruelty is aimed at a defenceless child, cast out by superstition that runs deeper than reason.Geralt acts, instinctively and perhaps foolishly. He takes the child under his protection. The Path is harsh, the world unforgiving, and hardly a place for someone who can’t survive it alone. But what begins as necessity slowly grows into something else: a quiet bond, forged in rain, campfires, and questions even a Witcher can’t answer.Winter leads them to Kaer Morhen, where the old ways still rule. Among brutal training and deep mistrust, what began beyond the walls must prove its worth. Kaer Morhen has never made room for what doesn't fit. And what doesn't fit has a way of changing everything.

Jaskier closes his eyes, but he nods. "I know. I'm not asking... I know you'll do anything to save her. I would too."
Don't say that. Don't make me pay for my child's life with yours.
It would be the most selfish thing in the world to say, the most hypocritical, and yet Geralt wants to anyway. Wants to be selfish in his love, because it is more worth protecting than anything else he's ever had.
"But," he says instead, "you were right before, and I'll swear it. I swear to you I would never leave you of my own choice. I will be with you as long as I am able, and as long as you'll have me." 
(They escape the rusalka and the swamp, but their fears follow them. Geralt and Jaskier turn to each other in the aftermath.)

After too many hunts, too many sleepless roads, and far too much monster guts in his hair, Geralt takes a rare, peaceful contract: guarding an herbalist’s garden from thieves.
No monsters, no curses, no chaos—just plants.
Jaskier calls it a holiday for his scowling face and insists on tagging along.

summary:
Years after the wars and the wanderings, Geralt and Jaskier still walk the roads — not to hunt, not to flee, but simply because neither of them knows how to stop.
There are no monsters left to fight, no contracts to chase. Just meadows, laughter, burned stew, and a long stretch of peace they never expected to earn.
As they drift from festivals to campfires and finally back to Kaer Morhen, they learn what it means to stay — to share quiet songs, gentle teasing, and a love that no longer needs to hide behind duty or danger.
The monsters are gone. The story goes on.
And for the first time, the road leads home.

summary:
“Freak.”
Geralt doesn’t flinch.It’s nothing he hasn't heard before, usually followed by a derisive laugh. The stranger might not have meant for him to hear the word, muttered as it is while Geralt's back is turned.Even when people have heard about Witcher Syndrome and know what to expect from it, they seem to forget about the more acute senses. So, he pretends that the insult was just an unconscious aside that the man behind him meant to keep to himself, and tries to continue his workout.———Witcher Syndrome is a disorder that causes genetic mutations to occur to those who develop it. While some symptoms could almost be considered advantageous, others are clearly detrimental to those affected. As with any disability, there are those with prejudices against those that are “other” or “different”.Geralt has spent most of his life learning to protect himself from those who won’t understand that his differences don’t make him a freak.
But, it will take someone with quite a lot of zest for life and self-love, to show Geralt how to be okay with himself, and to remind him that he is still only human.
Someone like Jaskier.
OR: What if superpowers were a disability?

When Geralt and Jaskier arrive in a riverside town stricken by a strange illness, they find that the sickness comes not from monsters, but from music — a haunting melody carried on the wind. summary:
Set in the 1920s, Julian Pankratz, known to most as Jaskier, prefers chasing melodies over titles, despite being the heir to a noble name and the son of a respected archaeologist.
One rainy morning at the university, Jaskier encounters a mysterious man with white hair and golden eyes—Geralt de Rivia, an "artifact retrieval specialist" who harbours secrets as deep as the relics he uncovers. Their brief but charged meeting proves to be fateful.
That night, Jaskier's world shatters when his father is murdered, leaving behind a mysterious ancient necklace as the only clue.
Consumed by grief and desperate for answers, Jaskier seeks the help of Geralt, a hardened treasure hunter known for surviving impossible situations. Though reluctant, Geralt is sworn to protect Jaskier and agrees to join him on a perilous journey. What begins as a quest for truth quickly escalates into a fight for survival, as they face ruthless killers and otherworldly forces while racing to uncover secrets that should have remained buried.

summary:
Yennefer's hand drifts over the rubbish bin, centimetres away from tossing the letter she holds into the trash (because seriously, who sends letters anymore?) when she freezes. It's addressed to Yennefer of Vengerberg, which is not surprising because that is who she is and yes, she does in fact live at the location designated below her name. The surprising part is the return address: Studio Aretuza, Thanedd Isle, Temeria.
There's a vaguely familiar logo stamped on the corner, a simple yet elegant trident dividing the letters H and K. It's the symbol of Hell's Kitchen, the television show. From what she can gather, the show is just another excuse for Tissaia to be even more of a rigid, neurotic control freak than she already is. Not exactly Yennefer's idea of a good time.
But... sheer curiosity gets the better of her. Deft hands swiftly tear open the envelope, unveiling the letter within before she can stop herself.

summary:
It is the first properly warm day of the year where Jaskier is free at the same time. Up until now, when the temperature has been warm enough to be outside, Jaskier has been stuck inside because of work or something as equally ridiculous.Today, he is free, and today is said to promise sun together with some good heat. So what is a young musician to do? He is to slather his entire glorious self with sunscreen, and then he is off to the subway and to the beach.
 
Geralt doesn’t understand Jaskier’s need to be in water, his craving to soak in the sun’s rays. He calls him a little seal and Jaskier huffs and puffs, but seals are at least cuter than fish. Much less slimy. Geralt has yet to agree, but that is just a matter of time. He always does.

Kaer Morhen has always been a fortress of solitary wolves—Witchers, feared and untouchable. But behind their steel and growls, they are a pride of omegas, starved for touch yet bound by duty. Geralt, Eskel, Lambert, Aiden, and even Vesemir hide their longing beneath sharp blades and sharper tongues, their instincts craving what they cannot ask for: an alpha’s claim.
Enter Jaskier—flamboyant, chaotic, and utterly oblivious to the way his presence makes the Witchers tremble. He’s just a bard tagging along for adventure, unaware that his laughter is a siren’s call to their suppressed needs. When winter forces them all back to Kaer Morhen, the fragile balance shatters. The Witchers’ restraint wears thin, and Jaskier? Well, he never expected to be the center of a lion’s den.
A story of hunger disguised as irritation, devotion masked in grumbles, and the slow unraveling of the last Wolf Pack’s control over their instincts—one bard’s terrible pun at a time.

summary:
Ciri was raised by her mother, Yennefer, while her father, Geralt, spent most of her childhood behind bars. Her parents’ brief union had led to her birth, but they were never truly together. Years later, Geralt remarried—a musician named Jaskier, whose wit and charm became the stuff of stories whispered through the years. But those same whispers also carried the scandal: Jaskier had been found dead in a bathtub, and Geralt was arrested for the crime, swearing his innocence until the day he was locked away.

summary:
It was a miracle that he had managed to return to the imperial palace; Well , the fact of being close enough to return with a sprint on horseback and that Roach remembered the path also helped. He was half slouched on Roach, sweating and gasping, even if he had swallowed a golden oriole, his vision was blurred, with spots and in perpetual undulation. The antidote was taken late, the poison will be neutralized, but it will have side effects.For now, the only things he could trust were; his hearing, touch, and smell.
His sense of smell was what led him to be attracted by a scent , not a known one or rather a recognizable one. Ciri, accompanied by Yennefer, had left the palace for the duties of future heiress, he believes. So, at first, he didn’t understand why his body still wanted to go there but slowly, he understoods. There was another reassuring fragrance, the odour of a person, whose his body was sure that, this one ,will keep him safe during a complicated situation, which is currently the case.
An injured Geralt follow a scent that bring him confort, to rest and heal in a safe place.

  “Jaskier!” She barks.Jaskier laughs, and leans forward, pushing her feet faster, eyes focused on her dazzling finish line. As she runs, she hikes up her dress, tying the length of it in a knot at her hip.Exhilaration pumps through her veins as she hears Geralt’s boots thump the ground behind her. Her own dig into the soft ground and spring off it easily.She makes it almost halfway to the stream before Geralt catches up with her, an arm slinging around her waist with all the force of colliding into a tree trunk.“Oof!” Jaskier exclaims as she’s collected against Geralt’s armored chest and they both hit the ground forcefully.Jaskier pants hard, legs and lungs burning with equal ferocity. She pushes up on her elbow and stops, her nose inches from Geralt’s. summary: The gods have grown weary of the power building within the world created after the conjunction of the spheres. In order to dull this power they separate the worlds once more and warp the majority of their power into an intricate magical lock to keep the spheres from rejoining, but every lock has a key. To keep this key from ever being used to join the worlds together again, they pluck individuals with specific talents and skills from points in time where the impact of their disappearance on the world they left would’ve been minimal.Their first reluctant recruit is taken after his quiet death in an unremarkable forest at the hands of a nameless thief. The wealth you have amassed, the faces you have met along the way, these were the things that made up a good life.Or, “Geralt, Ciri, Yennefer, and Truss react to reader being a rogue. Rogues devote as much effort to mastering the use of a variety of skills as they do to perfecting their combat abilities, giving them a broad expertise that few other characters can match. Many rogues focus on stealth and deception, while others refine the skills that help them in a dungeon environment, such as climbing, finding and disarming traps, and opening locks.When it comes to combat, rogues prioritize still over brute strength. A rogue would rather make one precise strike, placing it exactly where the attack will hurt the target most, than wear an opponent down with a barrage of attacks. Rogues have an almost supernatural knack for avoiding danger, and a few learn magical tricks to supplement their other abilities. Some rogues are known to be thieves or assassins.”

summary:
Finally, darkness has fallen on this shortest night of the year. Litha, the night of the summer solstice, a mythical night of celebration and magic. The villagers have lit the bonfires, and music and singing invites to dance and make merry. Soon, couples will jump the fire together, a good omen for their relationship if they succeed.
 
 
 
However, not everybody's eyes are turned toward the fires and the celebrating crowd in their best traditional garments, no. Two beautiful, identical-looking young girls with colourful flower wreaths in their hair gaze toward the dark shadow of the nearby forest. They nod at each other. Then, hand in hand, they sneak away from the bonfires and festivities. It cannot be long until midnight now, the magical hour when, for a very short time, the flower of the fern will bloom in the deepest, most magical parts of the wilderness. And they will find it.
 
 
OR: The night of the summer solstice goes very different for Coën and Cahir than planned.

Tiny amethysts glittered where the eyes should be, violet as her own, catching the light with every subtle movement of her hand.It was a claim written in precious metal, a promise forged in silver, a blatant declaration to anyone who cared to look that Yennefer of Vengerberg—the most fiercely independent woman he'd ever known, who'd fought tooth and nail for every scrap of autonomy—chose to wear his symbol so visibly upon her skin.

summary:
Geralt of Rivia never expected a healer to change the rhythm of his journey - but Elyndra does, and without ever trying to.
In the shadowed valleys of Velen, where monsters roam and war devours hope, Geralt meets Elyndra: calm, principled, and carrying a warmth that lingers like incense. What begins as an unlikely companionship deepens with each shared campfire, each silent understanding. She doesn’t challenge his solitude - she honors it. And slowly, without demand or pretense, she becomes part of the path.
Together, they seek traces of Ciri, face the Wild Hunt’s omens, and reckon with the unquiet ghosts of Geralt’s past - especially one in black and white. But this story isn’t about choosing between hearts. It’s about learning to be still with someone, even in a world that never stops burning.
Slow-burn. A love that grows like roots: quiet, steady, and true.

summary: A critical essay examining the philosophical and emotional inconsistencies in The Witcher saga. Often praised for its moral ambiguity and character complexity, Sapkowski’s work begins to unravel under closer scrutiny - especially in how it handles love, trauma, sacrifice, and consequence. This essay explores the gap between what the story claims to be and what it actually delivers, focusing on the arcs of Geralt, Yennefer, and the moral center that the saga too often sidesteps. Includes commentary on abortion, emotional coherence, and the mythologizing of dysfunction.

summary: A critical essay from a pro-life perspective on how Season of Storms and the wider Witcher saga portray abortion—not with moral nuance, but with ideological simplicity. Sapkowski, known for complex themes, here offers a one-sided narrative: abortion as empowerment, pro-life conviction as tyranny, and the unborn child as voiceless and invisible. This essay explores the literary and ethical consequences of that framing, contrasting it with Milva’s arc in Baptism of Fire, which proves Sapkowski can write with depth—when he chooses to.

summary:
How godsforsaken must the stars over Jaskier's birth have been, for the bard to be the last omega born in almost half a century?
For the bard’s whole life, he’s had to dodge alphas who never got to claim an omega of their own before they all started dying off. In the years since the bard left home, Jaskier has learned a great deal about the way of the world, not all of it lovely, but he wouldn’t trade any of the bad to be a captive under his parents iron rule again. They’d done their utmost to mold Jaskier into the perfect omega: a womb for breeding and a pretty face. Someone to be married off to a rutting alpha lord who wanted a whole gaggle of noble babies.
Everything Jaskier has never wanted to be, and being the last of a dying breed has stolen so much joy from Jaskier.
He knew that it was only instinct that drove alphas to covet and endeavor to breed with the bard. But Jaskier was his own person, godsdamn it, and ‘no’ should bloody well mean no.
So the bard hides out in the wilderness during his heats, all alone, horny, and bored half to death.
And for years it works. Until by chance, Jaskier is found by an alpha in the middle of his heat. An alpha witcher.

summary:
"Fuck!" he says when his foot slips on the algae-covered rock and hits the surface of the tidal pool. Or at least that is what he wants to say. In his low commander voice. Instead, it sounds more like 'Croak'. And, sure, he has been taken by surprise, but his voice ought not to sound that small and pathetic under any circumstances, right? Quickly, he withdraws his foot from the dark water that is glowing with those mysterious dots of silver light again. But why do the dots look bigger and much closer than before? And why does he feel so utterly strange and - different all of a sudden? Kind of like shrunk? And in a very wrong body? What the—
 
  "Fuckety fuck!" Cahir hears a voice from far above. Her voice. Yennefer of Vengerberg. "I told you idiot to watch your step! See what you've done!"
 
  He looks up at her, flabbergasted. She is glaring down at him, her beautiful purple eyes sparkling with a mixture of disbelief and anger.
 While on the run with Yennefer after the failed execution, Cahir is cursed. Good that Yennefer is a sorceress and will be able to break the curse in a jiffy, or will she?

Jaskier podejrzewa, że medycy zajmują się nie tylko leczeniem. Tymczasem na dworze księcia Aglovala szykuje się uczta z okazji jego zaręczyn z syreną Sh’eenaz.Czyli kolejna przygoda Geralta i Jaskra w alternatywnej czasoprzestrzeni wiedźmińskiego świata. Jest intryga polityczna, jest wątek romantyczny, jest też pewien zazdrosny o swoją panią gryzoń.A przy okazji jest dużo o dotyku o i tym, dlaczego czasem tak się go boimy, o bliskości i intymności niekoniecznie erotycznej, o zahamowaniach, wzajemności i empatii w relacjach. Oprócz opowiadania Andrzeja Sapkowskiego wielką inspiracją była dla mnie książka "Republika ciał. Eseje o wyzwoleniu" brytyjskiej eseistki Olivii Laing, a w niej wątek psychoanalityka Wilhelma Reicha, badacza emocji zapisanych w ciele i autora pojęcia "zbroja charakteru".

summary: Elfy w uniwersum wiedźmina? Teoretycznie – tajemnicze, pełne magii, nie bojące pobrudzić sobie rączek krwią dh'oine. W praktyce? Potraktowane przez autora jak tło dekoracyjne, a przez Redów jak jeszcze gorsze tło, tylko z lepszym wątkiem walki o wolność. Ich kultura? Prawie nie istnieje. Historia? Dziurawa jak skarpetki po trzecim praniu i równie logiczna. A Sapkowski, zamiast to ogarnąć, uznał, że lepiej poświęcić czas na opisywanie magicznych owulacji elfek wywoływanych ludzkim nasieniem. Także no. Priorytety.Ale od czego mamy fanfiki? No właśnie. Praca przedstawia moją osobistą wersję ich historii, bazowaną na książkach, choć siłą rzeczy pojawią się elementy z gier, które uznałam za wartościowe (Nigdy to co zrobiono z Loc Muinne, apfuu).Nazwy własne to głównie moje widzimisię, inspirowane różnymi elfickimi językami. I nie, nawet nie próbuję robić tego subtelnie. Jeśli czytałeś/aś Silma to od razu będziesz wiedział o czym mowaA i ja po prostu kocham elfy. I będę ich bronić do ostatniej kropli krwi. A raczej – do ostatniej estetycznie wyhaftowanej chusteczki.

summary: The English version of my story "Dom medyków", inspired by the short story 'A Little Sacrifice' by Andrzej Sapkowski.With love and many thanks to all the Baltic countries with their folklore, languages and songs.Wounded, Geralt finds himself in the medics’ house in Bremervoord, where he wakes up in rather unusual company. Jaskier suspects the medics might be involved in more than just healing. Meanwhile, at Prince Agloval’s court, a feast is being prepared to celebrate his engagement to the mermaid Sh’eenaz.In other words, another adventure of Geralt and Jaskier. There’s political intrigue, a romantic subplot, and a certain rodent jealous of his lady.At the same time, it’s also a story about touch—about why we sometimes fear it—about closeness and intimacy that isn’t necessarily erotic, and about inhibitions, mutuality and empathy in relationships.A major inspiration for me was "Everybody. A Book About Freedom" by British essayist Olivia Laing, particularly her discussion of psychoanalyst Wilhelm Reich, a researcher of emotions stored in the body and the author of the concept of the "character armor."Enjoy! :)

Geralt flinches a little, too exhausted to do much else about it even though it stings. “Tapetum lucidum is already fully formed,” says a voice he recognizes as Reidrich. “Color’s good. He’ll make it.”Geralt swallows an awful noise that sits on his tongue. His dry throat clicks.“Put money on it, then. I’ve got thirty on the Kaedweni one at the end of the row.”“More the fool you,” says Reidrich, and he releases Geralt’s eyelid. He blinks in a haze. The ceiling above whirls and doubles. The shadows in the room seem sharp enough to cut himself on. “He’s going to rupture something, his blood pressure’s too high.”A mumbled curse. “Brats let me down every season. And he’d look at the stars and he’d talk to someone who actually listened and he wouldn’t be staring up at that god damn chandelier.He knows something is wrong, in the back of his mind. He knows he should get up and do something, but when he tries to sit up, the world tilts on its axis, threatening to send him back down again.It’s when he finds himself absentmindedly gnawing at one of his boot laces that he realises he doesn’t have a choice anymore. Но есть один нюанс.________Примечание переводчика:Эта история красной нитью проходит сквозь строки оригинального сюжета, начиная от "Крови эльфов". Те, кто знаком с книгами А. Сапковского найдут несколько приятных отсылок к первоисточнику и характерам книжных героев, в остальном же произведение самостоятельное и не требует знания литературного оригинала. summary:
When two witchers show up in Oxenfurt summoning Jaskier home to Lettenhove immediately, he's confused but intrigued. For one thing, Lettenhove isn't "home" - the last time he saw it, and the rest of his family, was eighteen years ago. Why is he needed there so urgently? Why is his life suddenly teeming with witchers? What's the truth about his family? Why is he in danger? Is there even a decent tailor in Lettenhove? And will he recognise real love when he sees it?
  Jaskier is sure he can stretch three days to four, meaning he’ll be able to attend the ceremony at which he’ll be officially declared a Master of the Seven Liberal Arts, then disgrace himself thoroughly at the all-night party afterwards. After that, he doesn’t much mind leaving Oxenfurt. He’s not the type to hang around once a party’s over, and after four years in the city, he’s ready for new things. New people, new sights, new adventures. New things to write songs about, and new audiences to sing them to. New loves, new beds, new pleasures. He’s already bought a horse and ordered a travelling wardrobe, and while he didn’t intend Lettenhove to be the first stop on the fascinating journey of the rest of his life, it might as well be.

summary: The Wolf’s BrideIn a village at the edge of the dark woods, a bargain has stood for generations: each full moon, a girl is chosen as the Wolf King’s bride, given to the beast so that the village may know peace. None have ever returned. None have ever been mourned.When Geralt of Rivia arrives to fulfill a contract on the Wolf King, he expects a monster. Instead, he finds a village steeped in quiet complicity, an elder with too many secrets, and a bride who does not fear her fate. Yetta, the chosen girl, wears her red cloak like an omen and walks into the forest with her head held high—not as prey, but as something else entirely.But the Wolf King is not what the village believes. He is something older, more dangerous, and far more human than a mere beast. As Geralt unravels the truth—that the real monsters wear human faces, and the true horror lies in the choices already made—he finds himself caught in a tale with no lesser evil.In the end, a girl will go into the woods. A beast will await her. And a Witcher will ride away, knowing nothing has truly changed.

“She saved your life, Jaskier,” Geralt said, looking him in the eye. “I can’t let her die.”
He stepped forward, moving past Jaskier, and a hand shot out to stop him. “I can’t let you die,” Jaskier snapped, with the same desperate determination as every word he spoke.
Geralt could push past him and climb up the stairs to where Yennefer waited, hair askew and prepared to risk it all for this fucking djinn. It would be easy, thoughtless–Jaskier didn’t have the strength to stop him. Yet Geralt didn’t move. He stood there, Jaskier’s hand pressed over the slow beat of his heart.
	
 Yennefer is a beautiful sorceress, trouble and deeply in trouble, and Geralt has already decided to save her from the trouble of her own making when Jasker–loyal, foolish, troublesome Jaskier–stands between him and the witch and asks him to walk away.
Geralt, somehow, does.
It changes everything–and it doesn't change enough. Geralt makes a wish.

summary:
Radovid glanced warily between the scattered halves of Rience’s corpse and the route to the embattled Aretuza. He opted for the path of least danger and hastened to keep up with the others, muttering under his breath, “There goes my last chance.”
  
  
    The witcher’s stride didn’t pause, but he did look over at Radovid with a slightly raised eyebrow.
  
  
    “Jaskier suggested we get rid of Rience to prove ourselves to you.” Radovid angled his head over his shoulder in a way that vaguely indicated the burning body parts they’d just left behind. “But I guess you didn’t need us.”
  
  
    Geralt looked away — not back towards the body, but ahead toward his family. Yennefer and Jaskier walked and talked with their heads close together as Yennefer gesticulated between smoking school and Thanedd’s coast line. Cirilla scanned the horizon with one hand on her sword and the other hand in Jaskier’s grasp.
  
  
    “No,” Geralt agreed. “We don’t.”
  
Ciri was still in the cabin when Radovid showed up, and left it with him and Jaskier in tow. This tiny change in plans will change the course of history.

summary: He had waited on that mountain for three days, hoping against hope that the Witcher would return, that he would apologize, that he would sweep in and save Jaskier like some kind of hero from a ballad. And that was the worst part of it all. Jaskier had wanted to be saved. He had wanted Geralt to protect him, even after the man had made it painfully clear that Jaskier was nothing but a burden.“Stupid,” Jaskier whispered, his voice barely audible over the faint drip of water echoing in the cave. “Stupid, foolish, pathetic Jaskier. When will you learn?”------------------------------------------------------------His first thought, fragmented and fleeting, was that he had made a mistake. Touching the medallion had been a mistake. This was a mistake. But the thought was swallowed almost immediately by the pain, a tidal wave of agony that left no room for reason, no room for anything but survival.Then, as quickly as it had begun, the flames vanished. But the pain did not.---------------------------------------------------------------Yet, as his hands trailed over his arms, his chest, his face, he found nothing. His skin was smooth, unblemished, as if the blood wasn’t his at all.

summary:
Finding the scent of a succubus wasn't too hard for Regis, even though Beauclair was full of smells. Succubus smelled different than anything else. It was like a mix of the intoxicating scent of ginger wine and lust, almondy softness with something savory Regis couldn't name.
Regis materialized on the balcony of the succubus's home after making sure she was not with someone at this moment. He knocked on the door and waited. Not long after the door opened. A blonde succubus with a questioning expression was staring at Regis. She was beautiful, as succubi always were, with long golden hair spilling from her crown. Her goat-like legs were soft with dark blond hair, her pudgy belly peeking over the loincloth that hugged her curves. A few seconds later, her expression changed to a charming smile.
"Oh, darling, you surprised me, but what a lovely surprise it is. My name is Natanis. Who are you, my handsome stranger?"

Opening the door, however, Geralt was struck with an unfamiliar pang of panic as he took in the sight before him.Jaskier was curled up on the floor next to the bed, still naked and not even cleaned up from earlier. His face was streaked with tears, old and new, and he hadn’t even removed the gag despite having the use of his hands to do so. His arms were wrapped around his bent legs, his shoulders curled inward in a way Geralt had never seen him do.Geralt sped Witcher-fast to Jaskier, kneeling in front of him and dipping his head to meet Jaskier’s eyes. The bard blinked, looking as though he was about to reach out for Geralt but then stopped himself. In a voice so quiet it was even hard for Geralt to hear, Jaskier mumbled something through his gag. Quickly but gently, Geralt removed the silk.“I didn’t mean to,” Jaskier whispered, his gaze unfocused.

summary: Geralt was always gathering weeds. Some Jaskier immediately identified as poisonous: white thornapple, for example, its distinctive trumpet-shaped flowers spiraling open into delicate starbursts, the leaves of which he looked at with wariness after an ill-advised experiment during his not-so-distant wayward youth. Belladonna, too, he recognized, its soft purple-yellow flowers demurely downturned, deceptively plump black berries temptingly revealed where the plant’s pale green sepals parted. White baneberries, in contrast, looked about as toxic as they were, each protruding artery-red stem topped with a single eerily white berry which bore a dark little pupil staring wildly into nothing. Geralt collected delicately curving purple flowers and shining, tender clusters of red berries and craggy roots or creamy pale rhizomes so newly unearthed that damp clumps of dirt still clung to their protruding tendrils.

summary: Geralt had encountered many magical arts, but he hated portals the most. And he had good reasons for such hostility: every time he used a portal, something went wrong or he was sent to a place from which it was impossible to get out. His life was spoiled considerably, so he preferred the old method of traveling - to stomp on the native soil with his feet or to have horse hooves clatter under the saddle. His beloved Yen loved to laugh at his phobia, teasing him that even his adopted daughter was born with the gift of teleportation and now galloped through the worlds as she pleased. The witcher only grumbled discontentedly, but was not eager to quarrel with the sorceress, otherwise she would send him somewhere. This had already happened several times when Geralt got drunk with Lambert and Eskel, which Yen really did not like. But the portal still did not like the witcher. And they managed to take revenge in such a way that now all that was left was to scratch their heads...

summary: At the end of the war, with no clear winner and the leaders of both sides dead, Jaskier and Ciri are tired, alone, and less cautious than they really should be. Captured by Fringilla to be used as a sacrifice for a powerful ritual, Ciri realizes something that Fringilla, steeped in dark magic as she is, doesn't: This ritual does not have one caster and two sacrifices, it has three casters.Taking control of the spell Ciri and Jaskier end up decades back in time, in a world changed beyond their imagining. Navigating Redanian court and managing the Lettenhove Viscounty is exhausting unfulfilling work, but it's a price they're willing to pay for a world where Geralt can be happy.And then Redanian court threatens that happiness directly, and they end up at Kaer Morhen in an effort to keep an eye on the nobles looking to use the Witchers for their own gain. The longer they spend there, the more the entangle themselves with the people who used to be their loved ones, and the harder it is to hold back the fact that they're not exactly who they say they are.

summary: Magic is art, but daggers are brushes and blood is paint.Isbel aep Muir Moss is a sorceress. Under the Golden Sun banners she serves the Emperor. Her life doesn't belong to her, there are no choices in it. She lives only for Nilfgaard.The Witcher: The Coin of Life is a prequel to Andrzej Sapkowski's The Witcher saga. It follows a battle mage, the daughter of a soldier and a philosopher, in her effort to find her place in a world full of war and death. Six chapters resolve around the most important events of nilfgaardian history, from The Usurper's coup to The Battle of Sodden. Familiar characters from the books and games accompany her journey (such as Emhyr var Emreis, Triss Merigold, Cahir aep Ceallach or Queen Meve) and the few original characters shine with all the shades of nilfgaardian golden-black.Long live Nilfgaard! V šesti kapitolách se její příběh točí kolem nejvýznamnějších událostí nilfgaardské historie, od vojenského převratu Uzurpátora až po Bitvu o Sodden. Její příběh doplňují známé osobnosti z knih a her (jako jsou Emhyr var Emreis, Triss Rannuncul, Cahir aep Ceallach nebo královna Meve), ale i zcela nové postavy hrající všemi odstíny nilfgaardské černozlaté.Ať žije Nilfgaard! Ať žije císař!

summary:
Coën groans. Judging by how tired he feels, he cannot have slept for long, maybe an hour or two. Something has woken him up. A sound like the whetting of a blade. Cahir is not sharpening his sword in the middle of the night, is he? Groggily, he blinks his eyes open.
 
  "Hmm, how strange. This has never happened before. Why are you not out cold like your friend?"
 
  For a moment, Coën stares at the tall blonde man, disoriented. Then his memory clicks into place. Soren. The cottage in the heath. The delicious meal and the nice guest room with the one bed. Cahir snuggled up close to him. Fuck, this is not the bed he fell asleep in, he suddenly realises. It feels like he is lying on a wooden table instead, and his hands— Dammit, what is going on here? And where is Cahir?
 Coën and Cahir have found shelter from the thunderstorm in a shepherd's cottage and spent a nice evening there with Soren, its friendly owner. However, not everything is as it seems ... (Sequel to "Too Good to be True?")

Why did it have to be a dh’oine, not an elf? Why this particular dh’oine, the one who couldn't stand him? How did it make him feel? Would he change it if he could? In a way, it did make sense that they were tied together. They were an even match, a perfectly balanced pair, even if a pair of sworn enemies. “I've come to accept it,” he answered finally. And it was the truth, just not the whole picture.Whatever answer Roche was expecting, it clearly wasn't this one, for his expression turned grim again, mouth turned down at the corners in... disappointment? summary:
Jaskier's been having a lovely time having kinky D/s sex with Anna Henrietta all winter, but with the departure of his best friend and safety net, he questions if staying with Anna is a safe decision at all.
  
    
  Jaskier is nestled in the center of Anna Henrietta's regally appointed bed. Plush down quilts and pillows are tossed off to the side and the silk satin sheets rub pleasantly against his shins where they sink into the feather mattress. He is ensconced in the lap of luxury while the snow drifts softly outside. The owner of the well appointed bed (and the entire surrounding duchy) is settled behind him, evening out the satin ribbon lacing of Jaskier's corset before she starts to really tighten it. He can feel the slide of the ribbon and the tickle of her well manicured nails against his back. He's tense and the hairs at the nape of his neck raise. It's too much and not enough. summary: The Witcher’s heart stopped for a mere half of a second before it picked up speed that had him feeling almost human. The first thought that crossed Geralt’s mind was Neirblath and the second was an attempt to push and shove that first thought aside because he had not seen evidence of Neirblath in nearly three hundred years. The world was larger and not every iteration would appear on the Continent. Still, Geralt had often concluded that Neirblath’s influence on his life had run its course after the second convergence.“My name is Jaskier,” Jaskier offered.“Geralt,” the Witcher replied.Jaskier’s eyes darted down to the book of poetry before him before gazing back up with even wider eyes. “Wow, this is not a coincidence, is it?”With an almost suffering sigh, Geralt shook his head, “No.”The man bit his bottom lip hard as he stared at Dandelion’s tome. “I did my entire dissertation on Dandelion’s two tomes."A story in which Jaskier and Geralt's souls are bonded for eternity. Geralt has lived through many of Jaskier's lives and after 300 years of nothing, he suddenly appears, and Geralt wants nothing more than to have him again. Especially when he realizes Jaskier wants him too.

summary: Jaskier had a problem. Actually, he had two, quite interconnected problems. For now, he was focused on the more complicated one.The problem that sported a dashing smile, soulful eyes, and an immaculate heart.The problem currently examining Jaskiers fingers with rapt attention. The problem holding, nay, caressing them with his warm, large hands; as if they were the most precious of artefacts. “I told you, they are fine. What remains of the scars…” Jaskier stammered, his false bravado chipping away with every breath.“Regardless of its extent, you are suffering. The vile flames reached deeper than your skin. Even though the visible marks have faded, still the evil lingers. Whenever you play your lute, while your beautiful melodies remain untainted, your flesh pulses with malevolent pain. Why have you been hiding this?” The soft inquiry held an edge of rebuke. Jaskier raised his head. The honest gaze that met his own threatened to pull him down into its velvety depths, depths that would become his home. One that he may never wish to leave.Or, the Intersherical romance between a paladin and a bard no one had asked for.

summary: Dying was not a pleasant experience as books about fantastic heroes made it seem. It was not a noble, satisfying and peaceful ending for someone who had won his battles and died in a soft bed, with years of history and loved ones surrounding him.Nor was it the noble ending of dying in battle, where the hero defeated the monster before perishing with the certainty of having saved lives or at least tried. In the latter, the departure might have contained some anguish, but it was still serene.No. Jaskier, as an unwanted, hyperactive child and later a bard with no sense of self-preservation, felt death lurking more than once.Therefore, he could say from first-hand experience and with complete conviction, dying was absolute shit. (Jaskier is not literally dead)

Slavic Mythology & Folklore
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary: The Kingdom of Banska was hit by misfortune. A plague is rampaging and demolishing everything before it. Queen Vera and her court tried everything in their power. All hope has left. But who is knocking on the door?A short young woman with honey hair arrives and announces salvation. Her name is Zora and she claims to be a sorceress.Prince Radoslav  who also arrives at the court, perhaps is not a sorcerer himself, but someone very well acquainted with mystical powers. At the invitation of the queen, he supervises Zora, who has not yet won their trust.Will Zora save the people? Why her? Where did she get the medicine from?In short, "The Price of Power" is a story I write sometimes in my spare time. I decided to share it with the world because why not, if someone reads it I will give me more motivation to continue writing. The plot is set in a fantasy world of beings and gods, inspired by myths from the mythology of slavic nations and Croatian folklore and customs. In addition, it explores the dark side of human personality and the consequences that power leaves when it finds itself in the hands of an individual and the constructions and functions of religion and faith.

summary: Lambert was sitting at the bar minding his business when an all too familiar scent hit his nose and Lambert froze. He’d recognise that perfume anywhere - it was one of his, afterall.His products were pretty popular amongst the alternative crowd so it was kind of strange to realise Milena was wearing one of his perfumes.That particular scent was Lambert’s take on a classic rose fragrance. It smelled of dark roses, mossy earth, with an odd, cold metallic note that the blurb on his website likened to Sleeping Beauty pricking her finger.As far as openings go, he was never going to get a better one. So he steeled himself, took a sip of his drink, and steeled himself some more.“I like your perfume,” he managed to say without tripping over his tongue.“Oh, thank you,” Milena blushed. “It’s called Prick Your Finger,” she stammered slightly.Lambert grinned wolfishly, knowing full well that the label on the bottle only said PRICK but that Milena was too damn sweet to say it.

summary: Jaskier is finally free. After so long trapped in a form not his own he had begun to doubt which was his true self. But here he is, unshackled. The betrayals, violence, abandonment- the destruction his family wrought upon themselves and others, all of it left far behind. Jaskier is determined to enjoy this second chance. To bask in the beauty of life and ignore what horrors linger. Then he meets Geralt and things become complicated..........................................................“They don’t exist.”“Pardon?” The bard’s brown hair flops as he tilts his head.Geralt bravely doesn’t sigh again. “The monsters in your songs. They don’t exist.”For some reason that gets him a grin, “How do you know?”Geralt stares at him.“I’m a Witcher.”The bard laughs, “So just because you’ve never seen them that means they don’t exist?”“Yes.” Geralt says flatly.“Agree to disagree.” The man says flippantly, “But I would love to hear more about the monsters you’ve fought.”“No.” Geralt takes a drink desperately and finds he is almost at the bottom of his tankard. He contemplates whether it’s worth the coin for another. Probably not.

She was infected in their borders, she’s their responsibility. Contrary to popular belief, there can be more than one alpha in a pack, there just tends not to be because of how territorial they can get. Not all of them are as accepting of their new charge, one wants nothing to do with her past making sure she doesn’t go feral herself, but not for any care for her well-being. Feral wolves are dangerous and violent, the by-product of a person’s mind not being able to handle the transformation and breaking. summary: When Ciri first arrives at Kaer Morhen, Geralt is not father to her. He is destiny, protector—but he is new, and unpredictable. Ciri still dreams at night of running into Eist’s arms, letting him whisper her Skelliger lullabies until her heartbeat calms and she knows she is safe from the dark shapes that haunt her. She still dreams of riding on the saddle behind her grandmother, holding tight to her as she rides past the ominous form of the knight with the black-winged helmet and takes off his plumed head in one swing. In the dream, she can tell that her grandmother takes a savage delight in the act, in destroying what has caused Ciri fear. Ciri holds onto her, braces her hands against the solidity of her grandmother’s breastplate, lays her face against the blood and woodsmoke scent of her Cintran-blue cloak, and feels safe in the savagery.Geralt is not that for her. Still, he lets her go without speaking about it, does not prod, when she awakes sobbing from her dreams of long-dead comforts.-“What exactly is Kaer Morhen?”“It’s where witchers go in the winter,” he tells her, without skipping a beat, and then pauses. “It’s… like a home. You’ll be safe there.”

summary:
Yennefer and Dandelion continue their conversation at the inn. Dandelion is a bit of a sleaze but he's the one person she can really trust with Geralt and, surprisingly, her own feelings about the difficult Witcher.
  “You saved my life so now you’re responsible for it?” Dandelion’s tone was all levity, despite the seriousness of the matter. Yennefer’s responding laugh rang hollow.

  Dandelion leaned forward conspiratorially, chin settling on his hand. “I don’t make a habit of admitting to mistakes, but you did save my life. I’ve already thanked you and promised to rehabilitate your reputation, but I find it’s not enough. I was wrong about you.”

  “Oh?”

  “I thought you were cruel all the way through, but you’re scared and lonely just like the rest of us mere mortals.”

  Yennefer did not understand this man. She’d had plenty of opportunity to poke around inside his head and had found it to be so empty it echoed, yet she had read his poetry, heard his ballads, witnessed him say things like this.

Geralt snapped his teeth at him, just slow enough for Jaskier to retreat his hand in time.“Okay, no. That’s it, stop.” Jaskier said fiercely, not backing off. Geralt growled and snarled again.“I said no. Geralt, back off.” There was no hesitation to detect when Jaskier spoke. The Witcher shut his mouth with a click.“Good. Now look away.”When Geralt comes home from a hunt, he gets stuck in sensory-overload. He hasn’t slept in days, has not taken care of himself and deals with the burning toxicity of Black Blood in his veins. Jaskier has no clue about all of that and does what he usually does. And that is to take over control.

summary:
Ciri leaves Kaer Morhen. She doesn't understand why Geralt is bringing a bard with them. She doesn't want Geralt to bring a bard with them. 
  “You’ll spoil her,” Yennefer said. It was the first thing she had said all morning.

  Jaskier shrugged and petted the horse’s muzzle. “Him? It’s a gelding, so maybe not a him. Hm, in people having your balls cut off doesn’t make you not a man unless you want it to but you can’t ask a horse. Anyway, not a her. And better spoiled than mad at me.”

  “You’ll have both spoiled and mad at you when you run out of treats,” Ciri said, mostly to see what Jaskier would do.

  He smiled blithely at her. “We’ll cross that bridge when we come to it. No reason not to enjoy the apples while we have them, isn’t that right, Fredrick?”

  “That’s not…” Ciri trailed off and Jaskier looked at her quizzically. None of the Witchers would name their horse Fredrick, but Ciri didn’t know the gelding’s proper name, wasn’t even sure which of the now dead Witchers it had belonged to. She hadn’t spent enough time in the stables to learn these things but it still felt like a failure not to know.

summary: Next, Shani moved to check his eyes and pupils. A lot of diagnostic findings could be determined by their level of dilation and whether they reacted to the light. She pulled the left eyelid up and her breath was suddenly and completely taken away.  “What the hell,” she spat out, as she was greeted with a yellow orbit with a slit pupil, much like a cat’s, in this otherwise human face.  She stumbled back a few steps, and worked at catching her breath.  And then suddenly it all made sense: the gore, the immense stature, the apparent strength.  The man in front of her was a Witcher, harmed in the line of duty. Not enough Witchers were left to regularly come across them, and Cryptid 101 wasn’t exactly in her medical curriculum.***Shani is having an ordinary, though exhausting, day at the clinic, contemplating her future as she approaches the end of her medical training.  When a wounded Witcher is dropped at her doorstep, she needs to use all of her ingenuity to help the man, but becomes quickly suspicious when she finds him in possession of a lute, specifically her friend Jaskier’s lute. As is par for the course, she might make a few erroneous guesses…Stands alone, but also part of the Who are You series.

The witcher’s tone is even, and his face unexpressive, but Jaskier still tries to read into the words. As he walked the streets, the hood of his cloak mostly obscuring his face and hair, Geralt acquired an edge. He did not understand the sudden scorn, but he put his best foot forward, moving to push past it and this crowd. A staggeringly caustic scent caught Geralt's attention. It was subtle enough that only a witcher would pick up on it. But not just any witcher; it was a scent that only Geralt would know. It was bittersweet and had overwhelmingly familiar base notes. The horrible stench brought panic to his chest as he recognized the underlying accords of petrichor and parchment, drenched in pain.

summary:
Eskel returns every winter tightly wound, his thoughts all tangled up like old tack dumped on the stable floor. He hides it pretty well, or at least he thinks he does, applying his focus and remaining strength to the long list of chores that Vesemir hasn't managed to get to that year.
  There's no point pushing it in the first few weeks. Eskel will clam up and shrug it off. That big, booming laugh as he jokes his way out with a dry riposte shattering any hope of progress. Geralt bides his time. The comfortable bed and lack of action to keep Eskel occupied will wear him down enough to start faltering, to start dabbing at his scars, looking lost. summary: He was not pining, for gods’ sake. Jaskier did not pine.It was just… didn’t it all feel so… unfinished?There was that fateful night where Jaskier had purchased that glorious spell-in-a-bottle, which ended in Geralt wrecking him until he could hardly ride his gelding the next morning. That had been followed by a scant few weeks together on the road, burrowed together in bedrolls against the autumn air, reliving the bliss of Geralt’s touch on him, like fiery runes tracing down his ribs and spine and thighs.And then, what, Geralt off and disappears for the mysterious Kaer Morhen? No parting word on what the hell had happened between them, not so much as a “let’s do this again soon” or an “I’ll miss you”? Nothing beyond the affirmation that they would meet up again here once spring arrived, at the inn which they now parted ways? Hell, Jaskier would’ve taken a brisk “nice ass” before Geralt reined Roach down the left fork of the road as snow settled on the withered brown fields surrounding them, sentencing Jaskier to sleepless nights wondering just where it all left them.***AKA, Jaskier is pining for Geralt after getting railed by him in Deepest Desires

Young Geralt meets young Jaskier at Melitele's Temple.*
  On his very first day, a child with enormous blue eyes, a little younger than Geralt or simply shorter, starts following him around.

  Geralt is unnerved. There are other Witchers in training in Kaer Morhen, so it’s not like he isn’t used to being around kids his age, but they never mingle with civilians. Civilians need them, but don’t like them very much, Vesemir says, and Geralt suspects that to be a euphemism, a new word he just learned. A kindness. He’d seen the looks on people’s faces, how quickly they step away from them in the way you do when you put your hands too close to a fire. Witchers are useful, but dangerous, even the ones as young as Geralt. You wouldn’t adopt a wolf cub, knowing what he will grow into.

  Geralt’s efforts to avoid the child last an impressive ten minutes.

summary: Тяжелые грозовые тучи закрыли солнце, последний солнечный луч скользнул медным волосам Воорхиса, и во дворике потемнело. Вечерело, и аромат цветов становился интенсивнее, так что Ваттье стало будто бы нечем дышать – кровавые ноты теперь неприятно сдавливали виски и мешали думать о чем-то кроме того, как лезвие кинжала резко входит в плоть, и чужая кровь навсегда пачкает руки.«Морвран, - хрипло заговорил наконец де Ридо, но тут же исправился. – Правильнее будет, наверное, Ваше Величество?»Воорхис в ответ только отсалютовал кинжалом и расслабленно прикрыл глаза, вдыхая полной грудью сладкий запах роз, смешанный с холодом предгрозового воздуха.«Да, Ваше Величество… «Великое Солнце, осеняющее Континент» или что-то такое, я пока что не решил, - Морвран рассмеялся. – Да плевать, Ваттье, зови как хочешь… Мы же друзья?»Друзья, наверное. Ваттье тогда впервые увидел что-то безумное в глазах Морврана, но не придал этому значения. Перед глазами все еще стояла картина кровавого месива на ступенях Сената. Де Ридо собрался с силами и сдержанно кивнул.«Найди мне девчонку, - Морвран кинжалом срезал розу и заправил ее за ухо. – Если она не будет нашей, то будет чьей-то другой… Понимаешь?»

summary: “Be nice to me,” Jaskier panted on the floor, on his knees in front of his beautiful Witcher, already given up. He wasn’t going to fight back. Geralt was his. His his his, no one else's. They were alone in this cramped, dim room, filled with Geralt’s scent. Geralt smelled like a campfire and forest, roasted game, sweat, and rotten tripes. He always smelled like that after the hunt, and to Jaskier, it was the most alluring scent he could ever imagine. To him it signified protection. It meant love, it meant something safe to cling to in this cold, cruel world. Because Geralt would never leave him. Jaskier was sure he had tried, but if Jaskier couldn’t stop this anymore, neither did Geralt.

Radovid hummed."Elaborate on that.""Smart, cunning," Jaskier explained, teasing a finger down the side of Radovid's neck. "Crafty. Seemingly a harmless puppy, but you bite hard. Not afraid of a challenge. Leaner and not as tough as a wolf - but still very strong. And you have these sharp features and that reddish tint to your hair, so... a fox. Definitely."Well, Radovid could make do with that information. It planted a new image in his head - one where that sweet, eager bunny was hunted by not one, but two apex predators at once...It was as if Jaskier read his mind because he leant in really close to his ear and whispered "why? Would you like to join us?"

summary: Ciri wakes to a sob caught in her throat and a palm settled over her forehead.“Shh, darling,” someone murmurs to her, and it takes her a disconcertingly long amount of time to realize that it’s Jaskier. summary: Geralt understood perfectly well why Regis had not said goodbye to him. After all, the best way to keep a secret is to keep it to yourself and not entrust the mystery to anyone. Even a witcher can be coerced into revealing information if necessary; he knew this from personal experience. But if the witcher saw and heard nothing, then there was nothing to tell. Where did Emiel Regis go? Who the devil knows. In which direction did he go? Even if he had known, he would not have said. But surely some traces must have remained? Try tracking a higher vampire who wishes for only one thing - to disappear and for the entire world to forget his existence.Yes, Geralt understood it all. But, waking up on the banks of Sansretour in complete solitude, he still felt a sting of annoyance. As he sat, staring at the barely glowing embers of the campfire, a feeling of inner emptiness intensified.

summary: "You knew, didn't you?" he asks her.She sniffs. "There aren't many witchers. You're pretty recognisable, in all that beskar. And there are only so many who are wolves, and you all have slightly different wolves on your armour, and yours is the white wolf. I'm not stupid."He dips his head to her. "Princess Cirilla -""It's Ciri," she interrupts. "My name is Ciri. I'm your daughter by the law of surprise."Her hair is white, like her mother's. The way she stares him down is Calanthe, through and through. The way she'd followed through in Brokilon - Duny. The knucklebones she's flicking with in her pocket - click click click - are all Eist. summary: Snippets of memories flash through his head, almost too swift to register. Familiar yellow eyes. An ugly smirk. The glint of a fellow cat's medallion in the sun. The sound of heartbeats surrounding him. The burning agony of a poisoned blade sliding home in his gut. Then, nothing. Absolutely nothing.The cat witcher slowly moves a hand to his abdomen and gasps at the flare of pain as his hand touches blood-drenched fabric. Not leather. He's been stripped of his armor. Gloves, too. He doesn't even have to reach back for his swords to know they're gone as well - they would be digging into his back if they were there. They even took his fucking boots.Jad and his band tried to kill him, stripped him of all his belongings, and-A dawning horror causes the blood to freeze in his veins. It all makes sense now, even to his addled brains. The cramped quarters, the pine box, the muffled world around him. Aiden of Skellige has been buried alive.

His blade is sliding into Gallatin's throat, a look of betrayal etched into the elf's eyes while he struggles to breathe as blood floods his trachea and down his neck-Except that's not what happens at all.No, instead, in a stunning twist of fate and a show of skill that he thought not even Gallatin was capable of, Cahir's knife is ripped from his hand by the blade as it nears Gallatin.
